extracted.intended_audience: life-science researchers and authors seeking journal-independent peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policies for submitting and running journal-independent, pre-submission peer review (Review Commons) in the life sciences that produces a Refereed Preprint with one round of referee reports and an author response, and that facilitates transfer to bioRxiv and affiliate journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Commons will only review well-developed scholarly research papers that represent a clear advance for the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A managing editor in conjunction with an academic editorial board makes this decision independently of the selection criteria of affiliate journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews submitted to Review Commons cover the whole manuscript rather than partial sections or abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity known to editor/service
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identity known to Editor or service
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are known to the managing editor/service (i.e., not completely anonymous to the platform); the page does not state that reviewer names are publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests checked
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service checks for competing interests as part of the review workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response allowed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may provide a response to the referee reports; the Refereed Preprint includes the manuscript, referee reports from a single round of peer review, and the authors’ response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Commons does not make an editorial decision on publication; it provides refereed preprints and facilitates journal submission, leaving editorial decisions to journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who requests review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors initiate the review request to Review Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who selects reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selected by: Editor, service, or community
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An independent Managing Editor will liaise with authors and assign experienced professional editors (EMBO Press) to run the in-depth peer-review and invite referees; EMBO editors invite referees but will not assess the manuscript for their journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-reviewing allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may co-review manuscripts with colleagues, e.g., members of their research groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-reviewing is explicitly permitted, enabling collaborators or group members to participate in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-round peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Refereed Preprint includes reports from a single round of peer review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Refereed Preprint contains the manuscript, reports from one round of peer review, and the authors' response; Review Commons aims to provide a single, high-quality round to reduce serial re-review at multiple journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow reviewers to focus on the science, not specific journal fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are encouraged to evaluate scientific merit and clarity rather than appropriateness for a particular journal, with the aim of producing reports useful across journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript hosting / transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript hosting: No; Review Commons transfers Refereed Preprints on behalf of authors to bioRxiv and affiliate journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service does not host manuscripts long-term but facilitates posting to bioRxiv and transfers to 17 affiliate journals (EMBO Press, PLOS, eLife, Rockefeller University Press, The Company of Biologists and ASCB). It also facilitates author-directed submission to affiliate journals to expedite editorial consideration and reduce serial re-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency — open reports
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project encourages transparency by enabling posting of reviews and authors’ replies to bioRxiv and will monitor the fraction of authors who post their reviews and replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics to evaluate the service: submission rate, time from submission to publication, and average number of reviewers needed per published manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics are used to assess engagement, efficiency, and the effect of Review Commons on reducing repeated re-review; the platform will monitor submission rate (engagement), time to publication (efficiency), average reviewers per published manuscript (efficiency), and fraction of authors posting reviews/replies (transparency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of editorial management
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent Managing Editor assigns experienced professional editors at EMBO Press to run a high-quality, in-depth peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO editors act as managers who invite referees but explicitly will not use the review process to assess the manuscript for their own journals, preserving neutrality.
